draft.title: Health status indicators
card: A health status indicator is a measure that describes how healthy a population is. Governments use indicators to see how health is changing and where help is needed.
the average number of years a person born in a given period could expect to live, if current death rates stayed the same.
deaths in a population. It is often given as a rate, such as deaths per 1000 people, so groups of different sizes can be compared.
the amount of illness, disease or injury in a population. Self-assessed health status is how people rate their own health, for example as excellent, good or poor.
draft.remember: Indicators measure a population's health by length of life, deaths, illness and how people rate their own health.

a.q: Which health status indicator describes how much illness, disease or injury is in a population?
a.why: Morbidity is the amount of illness, disease or injury. Mortality is the tempting wrong answer, because it also describes poor health, but it counts deaths and not illness.

b.q: A health report in Victoria says that 70% of adults in a town rate their own health as good or better. Which indicator does this show?
b.why: The adults are rating their own health, which is self-assessed health status. Morbidity is tempting because the report is about health, but morbidity counts illness, disease or injury and does not come from people's own ratings.
b.clue: Who is judging the health in this report?
